evidence_passages.text:
**Supported facts**

As of **August 27, 2026**, Apple’s security-releases index says **“The latest version of macOS is 26.6.2”** and lists **`macOS Tahoe 26.6.2`** with a **release date of August 17, 2026**.  
Source: https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100

Apple’s security-releases index also lists a newer **Mac-related** security release, **`Safari 26.6.1`**, dated **August 18, 2026**, and says it is available for **macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia**.  
Source: https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100

Apple’s security-content page for **`macOS Tahoe 26.6.2`** says the update was **released August 17, 2026** and is **“Available for: macOS Tahoe.”**  
Source: https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281

That same Apple page lists the vulnerabilities fixed in **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2**, including entries in **Audio, ImageIO, IOGPUFamily, Kernel, WebKit, WebKit History, and WebKit Storage**.  
Source: https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281

Apple’s security-content page for **`Safari 26.6.1`** says it was **released August 18, 2026** and is **“Available for: macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia.”**  
Source: https://support.apple.com/en-us/148286

That Safari page lists WebKit-family fixes only.  
Source: https://support.apple.com/en-us/148286

**Inference from those facts**

If you mean **the most recent macOS operating-system security update**, the answer is **`macOS Tahoe 26.6.2`** for **systems running macOS Tahoe**. This is the strongest reading because Apple’s index separately says the **latest version of macOS is 26.6.2**.  
Sources: https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100 , https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281

If you mean **the most recent security update affecting Macs**, regardless of whether it is the OS itself, then the newest one listed is **`Safari 26.6.1`** for **macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia**.  
Sources: https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100 , https://support.apple.com/en-us/148286

**Actively exploited issues**

I found **no Apple statement on either page identifying any actively exploited issue** in **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2** or **Safari 26.6.1**.  
This is an **inference from absence**: on the two Apple security-content pages above, Apple lists the CVEs and impacts, but the pages do **not** include Apple’s usual exploitation wording such as “Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been actively exploited.”  
Sources inspected: https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281 , https://support.apple.com/en-us/148286

**Uncertainty / ambiguity**

There is a real ambiguity in the phrase **“most recent macOS security update.”** Apple’s own index supports **two different answers** depending on whether you mean:
1. the newest **macOS OS** release: **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2**; or  
2. the newest **security release for Macs**: **Safari 26.6.1**.  
Source: https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100

**Bottom line**

Best-supported answer: **Apple’s most recent macOS OS security update is macOS Tahoe 26.6.2, affecting macOS Tahoe, and Apple does not identify any actively exploited issues on its security-content page for that update.**  
Sources: https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100 , https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281
